rationale: Chlorpromazine (high anticholinergic/antihistaminergic FGA) to risperidone (low anticholinergic SGA). The reduction in anticholinergic burden is significant — risperidone has minimal muscarinic activity. This means cholinergic rebound from CPZ withdrawal is NOT attenuated by risperidone (unlike the CPZ→olanzapine or CPZ→quetiapine switch). Cholinergic rebound symptoms must be anticipated and managed explicitly. The QTc risk from CPZ will decrease but risperidone also has moderate QTc prolongation. EPS profile moves from low-potency FGA (more sedating, less EPS) to moderate-potency SGA (more EPS than olanzapine/quetiapine). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start risperidone 1 mg. Continue chlorpromazine 400 mg. ECG at baseline. Warn about cholinergic rebound as CPZ is tapered — risperidone does not attenuate muscarinic rebound.
Increase risperidone to 2 mg. Plateau chlorpromazine. Allow risperidone to establish before tapering CPZ.
Increase risperidone to 4 mg (target). Reduce chlorpromazine to 300 mg. Cholinergic rebound likely — nausea, insomnia, diaphoresis.
Reduce chlorpromazine to 200 mg. Monitor QTc — additive risk during overlap though reducing as CPZ dose falls.
Reduce chlorpromazine to 100 mg. Prolactin rising on risperidone — monitor for sexual side effects.
Reduce chlorpromazine to 50 mg. EPS review — risperidone has more EPS burden than CPZ at these doses.
Stop chlorpromazine. Continue risperidone 4 mg. Repeat ECG at 4–6 weeks. Review EPS and prolactin.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Chlorpromazine 400 mg ≈ risperidone 4 mg (CPZ-equivalence: 100 mg CPZ ≈ 1 mg risperidone per Maudsley 15th). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
